name: Finazzi-Agrò PTNS versus sham
question: Does percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation improve urge incontinence in women unresponsive to behavioral and rehabilitation therapy or antimuscarinics compared with sham treatment?

design.population: 35 women with urodynamically confirmed detrusor overactivity incontinence unresponsive to behavioral and rehabilitation therapy or antimuscarinics.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 2002-2003; Appendix, p 2006

verdictNote: The primary responder endpoint met the prespecified two-sided 0.05 threshold in 32 completers.
takeaway: Among women with urodynamically confirmed detrusor overactivity incontinence after conservative treatment, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation yielded a 50% or greater reduction in urge-incontinence episodes in 12/17 completers versus 0/15 with sham (P < 0.001).

reports.label: End-of-treatment randomized report
reports.citation: Finazzi-Agrò E, Petta F, Sciobica F, et al. "Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation Effects on Detrusor Overactivity Incontinence are Not Due to a Placebo Effect: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled Trial." *J Urol.* 2010;184(5):2001-2006. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2010.06.113
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 2002-2003

results.measure: 50% or greater reduction in urge-incontinence episodes after 12 sessions, among completers
results.note: Prespecified primary outcome; chi-square 16.9 (df 1), P < 0.001 against two-sided alpha 0.05; 17/18 PTNS and 15/17 sham participants analyzed. No between-arm effect estimate or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 2002-2003; Results, p 2003

results.note: P value in effect is the treatment-by-time interaction; no between-arm effect estimate or confidence interval reported.

harms.label: Serious side effects and stimulation-site pain

values.exp: No serious side effects; occasional transient stimulation-site pain (count not reported)
values.ctl: No serious side effects; occasional transient stimulation-site pain (count not reported)

delivery.label: Treatment schedule, stimulation and sham procedure

values.exp: 12 PTNS sessions; 34-gauge needle about 5 cm above medial malleolus, medial calcaneal surface electrode; Urgent PC, 9 V, 20 Hz, 0-10 mA titrated to toe movement and tolerance
values.ctl: 12 sham sessions; 34-gauge needle in medial gastrocnemius; current on for about 30 seconds, then off

delivery.note: Sessions lasted 30 minutes, three times weekly in both groups; allocation guesses after three sessions agreed with assignment approximately 60% of the time (19/32, calculated from Table 2; kappa 0.18, P = 0.305).
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 2002-2003; Results, p 2003; Table 2, p 2004

delivery.label: Noncompletion unrelated to technique
delivery.note: The responder analysis included 17 PTNS and 15 sham completers.
